text.title: Schema Pair Record — Output Contract
text.summary: The artefact this methodology produces: a Schema Pair Record (SPR) as YAML or JSON, machine-checkable by the bundled validator. It carries both schemas inline so the drop set is computed, not asserted.

schema.field: What the model is being asked to emit, in one line.
Providers this schema is sent to. Each item is `anthropic`, `gemini`, or `other`. `other` additionally requires `unsupported_keywords`.
Required only when `transports` contains `other`: the keyword list that transport does not compile, taken from its own docs with a fetch date.
Repo path of the file actually sent to the provider.
Repo path of the full-contract schema enforced after parse. MUST differ from `wire_schema_path` (r2).
The full contract inline — every constraint the output must satisfy.
The wire copy inline — supported keywords only. The validator diffs it against `validation_schema` to compute the drop set.

One entry per computed drop. Each item: `keyword`, `field` (JSON pointer), `on_violation` (`drop` | `reject` | `clamp`), `enforced_by` (code location that re-checks after parse), `counter` (metric name the check increments).
Constraints restated in a field `description` as prose for the model's benefit only. Explicitly NOT enforcement (r6). Each item: `keyword`, `field`, `text`.
Whether this request sets `output_config.format` or a strict tool schema.
Whether this request enables `citations` on any user-supplied `document` or `search_result` block.
How the 400 fork is resolved. `two_call` requires `two_call_note`.
Required when `citations_plan: two_call`: which call selects identifiers under a schema and which call produces cited prose over exactly those bodies.
Metric names computed over an eval run. MUST include `schema_valid_rate` AND at least one name that also appears as a `counter` in `dropped_keywords` (r7).
Where review budget goes now that compliance is not the bottleneck — the fields whose VALUES are checked by a human or a harness.

section.title: Per-transport dropped keywords (dated)
section.statement: Anthropic, docs fetched 2026-08-03 — not compiled: `minimum`, `maximum`, `exclusiveMinimum`, `exclusiveMaximum`, `multipleOf`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, `maxItems`, `uniqueItems`, and `minItems` other than 0 or 1. Compiled: types, `enum` of scalars, `const`, `anyOf`, `allOf` without `$ref`, internal `$ref`/`$defs`, `required`, `additionalProperties: false`, `default`, and a fixed list of string `format` values. Gemini, docs fetched 2026-08-03 — compiles an OpenAPI 3.0 subset that DOES accept `pattern` and numeric ranges, so its drop set is smaller and the two transports disagree. Re-verify both lists before any release that depends on them; Anthropic's list moved twice in the nine months to 2026-08-03.

section.title: Consistency rules the validator enforces
section.statement: The drop set is COMPUTED as (constraint keywords in `validation_schema`) minus (the same keyword at the same field in `wire_schema`); every computed drop must have a `dropped_keywords` entry, and every entry must correspond to a computed drop — no phantom bookkeeping. No keyword unsupported by any declared transport may remain in `wire_schema` (r6). `enforced_by` must be a code location, and a value that merely logs is rejected (r3). `structured_output` and `citations_enabled` must not both be true (r5). `metrics` must contain `schema_valid_rate` plus at least one declared counter (r7). `wire_schema_path` must differ from `validation_schema_path` (r2).
